cuerpo: 000 ABNT20 KNHC 201138 TWOAT Tropical Weather Outlook NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL 700 AM EST Fri Nov 20 2026 For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America: Offshore of the Southeast U.S. Coast: Surface observations indicate that a broad low pressure area is now located near the east coast of central Florida. The low is currently producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms extending from the central Florida peninsula east-southeastward over the Atlantic. This system could acquire subtropical or tropical characteristics while it moves generally northward to north-northeastward near or just offshore of the southeastern United States coast through the weekend. Regardless of subtropical or tropical development, the system is expected to produce strong gusty winds, dangerous surf, rip currents and coastal flooding along portions of the southeast and mid-Atlantic U.S. coasts into early next week. In addition, heavy rainfall and the threat of flash flooding will continue across portions of the Florida peninsula today, potentially spreading northward toward coastal portions of the Carolinas and the mid-Atlantic over the weekend.
